svg.title: Mersad Moghaddam — Software developer portfolio
svg.desc: Go and Linux software developer. Selected work: ClipDeck, Whisper Social, AetherDB, Argus and SysKit. Understand the problem, make deliberate choices, and learn through building. Project and contact links follow this illustration.

svg.title: Mersad Moghaddam — Software developer
svg.desc: I like building useful software. I work mostly with Go, developing backend services and tools for Linux. I enjoy understanding how things work and turning that understanding into software that solves practical problems.

svg.title: ClipDeck — Your clipboard, with a memory.
svg.desc: Your clipboard, with a memory. A clipboard manager for Linux that keeps what you copy searchable and within reach, with persistent history and a keyboard-first workflow. Conceptual CLI illustration.

svg.title: Whisper Social
svg.desc: A social backend that processes timeline updates in the background using Redis Streams, keeping post creation separate from the work of updating followers’ feeds.

svg.title: AetherDB
svg.desc: A key-value store where I explore how storage works, from memory-mapped files and concurrent indexing to zero-copy reads with sendfile.

svg.title: SysKit
svg.desc: A read-only terminal tool for exploring Linux system information. It reads from /proc, /sys, and Netlink directly, without relying on external shell commands.
svg.text: A read-only terminal tool for exploring Linux system
information. It reads from /proc, /sys, and Netlink directly,
without relying on external shell commands.

svg.title: How I work — Keep it simple. Keep learning.
svg.desc: Understand the problem. I like figuring out how things work before changing them. Reading the code and tracing the behavior help me choose what to build or fix. Make deliberate choices. I aim for code that is easy to follow, with clear responsibilities and sensible limits. Extra complexity should have a reason to be there. Learn through building. These projects are a way to solve useful problems and deepen my understanding. I test ideas, look at the results, and improve as I learn.
